body:
Conceptually this makes sense to me.

All changes except the last look good. For the last change, I have two comments.

Perhaps
```
if (!get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)) {
```
should be changed to 
```
if (!is_mouse && !get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)) {
```

I didn't test, if in `get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)` the coordinate system of `pos` is correct for `has_point`.

> Perhaps
> 
> ```
> if (!get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)) {
> ```
> 
> should be changed to
> 
> ```
> if (!is_mouse && !get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)) {

I agree with your suggested change, so I have applied it. 

> I didn't test, if in `get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)` the coordinate system of `pos` is correct for `has_point`.

I have tested if `pos` is correct with some print statements before this part:
```cpp
if (!is_mouse && !get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)) {
	// Skip this event if it is a touch event and the event position is outside of the viewport
	continue;
}
```
To make sure `pos` is relative to the viewport size and not the window size I made a new project, set the Viewport Width and Height to something smaller than my screen resolution (I set it to 200x200), set `display/window/stretch/mode` to `"viewport"`, set `display/window/stretch/aspect` to `"keep"` and exported it to my Android phone.

Then I checked by touching on a few spots. In my testing the `pos` x and y values ranged from 0.0 to 200.0 when I touched inside the viewport, and went above and below that range when I touched outside the viewport, so they seem right to me. I also printed the output of `get_visible_rect().has_point(pos)` and the output of that aligns with my findings, it being `true` when the `pos` x and y values were inside the 0-200 range, and `false` if either x or y was outside of that range.

This is just my testing though, so I understand if it needs to be tested by someone else to make sure it is right.
